Welcome
Walton High - A Place to Belong, a Place to Learn, a Place to AchieveAt Walton High, we are committed to ensuring that every student feels valued, supported, and inspired. We believe that a strong sense of belonging is the foundation for success, empowering young people to grow in confidence, embrace new opportunities, and achieve their full potential. Walton High is more than a place of learning; it is a vibrant and inclusive community where every individual is respected, encouraged and challenged to be their very best. We are ambitious for all our students. Whether in the classroom, on the sports field, through creative and performing arts, or in leadership and service opportunities, we foster excellence and celebrate achievement. Our curriculum is designed to challenge, engage and inspire, develop curiosity, resilience and a lifelong love of learning, while equipping students with the knowledge, skills and character they need to thrive in a rapidly changing world.As the world continues to evolve, our aim is not only to prepare students for their future, but also to empower them to shape it. We want our students to leave Walton High with confidence, compassion and a strong sense of purpose, ready to make a positive difference in their communities and beyond. Thank you for visiting our website. I hope it gives you a sense of the values, opportunities and achievements that make Walton High such a special place. I warmly invite you to explore further and discover all that our school has to offer.Jim Rowland, Principal
5 Dimensions Trust
We are a Multi-Academy Trust that serves the young people of west Milton Keynes, currently comprising of three secondary schools; The Hazeley Academy, Shenley Brook End School and Walton High and three primary schools; Priory Rise School, Emerson Valley School and Merebrook Infant School.

Careers
Every young person should leave school well prepared for life beyond their studies. High-quality careers education, information, advice and guidance play a key role in ensuring that students are equipped with the knowledge, skills and confidence needed to progress successfully into further education, training or employment.
Our careers programme is designed in line with the Gatsby Benchmarks of Good Career Guidance, ensuring students have access to a structured and progressive programme that supports them in understanding the full range of opportunities available to them. We aim to provide clear information, impartial advice and meaningful experiences that enable students to make informed decisions about their subject choices and future career pathways.
Through our PSHE curriculum, careers activities and engagement with employers, further education providers and training organisations, students are supported to explore different sectors and pathways. These experiences help them develop a deeper understanding of the world of work and how different education and training routes can lead to a variety of career opportunities.
Our goal is to inform, inspire and motivate students so they can confidently plan their next steps and recognise how the decisions they make today can shape their future.

Unifrog
Walton High students and parents have access to Unifrog, a comprehensive careers and destinations platform designed to support students across all year groups.
Students use Unifrog during tutor time and PSHE lessons, where they are guided through activities that help them explore their interests, understand different career pathways, and research future education and employment options. In addition to structured use in school, students can also access the platform independently in their own time to continue exploring courses, apprenticeships, and career opportunities.
Parents and carers are also able to create their own Unifrog accounts. This allows them to explore the same up-to-date information and resources as their child, helping them to support discussions about subject choices, further education, and future career plans.
Unifrog is designed to support learners in making informed decisions about their futures, with a range of tools that are suitable for all year groups. Each student has their own account that provides a range of information related to their interests and aspirations.
Key features of the platform for students include:
Students can log in from any computer, tablet, or smartphone. We encourage parents to use the platform with your child so you can support them through the process of deciding on their next steps.
You can create your own parent account where you’ll be able to see what your child is doing on Unifrog, including any interactions tagged against their name and any upcoming events we’ve logged for them. You’ll also be able to use all the same tools your child can to support them on their Unifrog journey.
You can open your account using your email address or using Single Sign-On with a Microsoft or Google email account. If you have any issues signing in, please contact Mrs Montague by emailing careers@wh5d.com.
You’ll also have the option to sign up to Unifrog’s parent newsletter to get expert advice and guidance on supporting your child with their next steps.

Personal, Social & Health Education
PSHE – Curriculum
The PSHE curriculum at Walton High School is fully statutory compliant and age appropriate for all of our students.
There are three core themes to our PSHE curriculum:
Intent, Implementation, Impact
There is now definitive evidence that shows students who are mentally and emotionally healthy do better at school. This is both academically and with the amount of extra-curricular activities they are involved with.
Therefore, our PSHE curriculum is tailored to the specific needs of the students who attend our school to ensure that they feel happy and supported at school which allows them to feel that this is a school where they belong, can learn without hindrance and achieve to the best of their abilities.
PSHE is a timetabled lesson at KS3 and KS4 with it being delivered as part of the tutor programme for KS5 students.
Students in each group in the school cover one topic each half-term and all lessons are well researched, resourced and are age appropriate. Staff receive regular CPD to support the teaching of the curriculum that has been provided by the PSHE lead, the safeguarding team and external agencies. There is also drop-in sessions available to those who teach PSHE should they need guidance or support in the delivery of the curriculum.
Lessons are quality assured by the PSHE lead and members of the senior team and we are very ambitious in the outcomes we want our students to achieve from the PSHE curriculum.
PSHE helps our students to achieve their potential by supporting their wellbeing and tackling issues that can have a negative effect on their ability to learn such as stress, anxiety and unhealthy relationships.
PSHE also allows students to develop skills such as teamwork, communication and resilience that are crucial to navigating the challenges and opportunities of the modern world and which are increasingly valued by employers.
Relationships and Sex Education Policy
The statutory guidance for RSE and Health Education came into effect in all secondary schools from 2020. This includes academies, free schools and independent schools.
In secondary education:
British Values are a fundamental part of the PSHE curriculum. British Values are:
Teaching British values in PSHE is vital because it prepares students to thrive in modern society, actively promotes respect for diversity, an understanding of the law, and the critical life skills needed to become responsible, active, and well-rounded citizens.
Integrating fundamental British values into PSHE equips our students for life beyond the classroom by building a strong moral compass and ensuring safety and inclusivity.
Spiritual, Moral, Social, Cultural (SMSC)
The promotion of the Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural development of our students in PSHE ensures that PSHE is not just a simple list of rights and wrongs. Instead, it builds character in our students and encourages them to make the correct choices for the correct reasons. We promote these values in the following way:
Personal, Social, Health, and Economic (PSHE) education serves as the preventative foundation for safeguarding in schools. While safeguarding involves reactive child protection procedures, PSHE proactively equips children with the knowledge and resilience to understand boundaries, recognise risks, and seek help.
PSHE and safeguarding are heavily intertwined, as both aim to identify and prevent potential harms. Core connections include:
The PSHE lead at the school is DSL trained and works closely with the safeguarding team at the school to both shape the curriculum and respond to any concerns that arise from the lessons and topics being taught.
There is a regular meeting between the PSHE lead and a member of the safeguarding team where the impact of the curriculum, work with external providers and agencies and current trends in the welfare of students is discussed with actions coming from each meeting.
Teaching Approaches
We have a consistent and joined up approach in the delivery of the PSHE curriculum across the school. Each student in the school will cover six topics during an academic year and these will be taught in the same order and at the same time. There is also an expectation that all staff use the central resources but that they also amend and adapt them for the needs of their class and individual students within that class. All staff follow the core principles of the delivery or our curriculum which include:
Interactive and Participatory Methods:
Evidence based and balanced delivery:
A progressive and tailored curriculum:
Establishing a Safe Space:
Inclusivity and Diversity
Integrating inclusivity and diversity in PSHE involves ensuring all students feel valued, safe, and represented. It moves beyond teaching mere tolerance to actively celebrating differences, challenging prejudice. We try and ensure this in several ways:
Assessment and Monitoring
The assessment and monitoring of PSHE ensures that learning is robust, students attitude and effort is tracked, and the curriculum effectively meets the statutory needs of our students. Unlike examined subjects, assessment in PSHE focuses on students personal growth, the skills they are expanding, and exploring attitudes rather than ‘passing or failing’.
The way we ensure this happens is through:
Learning Walks and observations: Regular drop-ins to check classroom environment, safety agreements, and student engagement.
Work Scrutiny: Reviewing of students booklets to check for coverage, understanding and depth of knowledge.
Student Voice: Speaking directly with students to ensure the curriculum feels relevant, engaging, and safe.
Staff Feedback Surveys: Analysis of staff confidence levels and tracking Continuing Professional Development (CPD) needs and requirements.
Attitude and effort tracking: Students receive an attitude and effort grade at several points during the academic year and this is communicated to parents/carers and the students themselves.
Parental engagement in Personal, Social, Health, and Economic (PSHE) education is an essential partnership that helps safeguard children and reinforces learning. When schools actively involve parents and carers in the PSHE and Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) curriculum, it creates a supportive environment and ensures families are aligned on the values being taught. There is complete transparency in the topics that are being taught and the rationale for why we teach them.
We consider parental engagement to be of the upmost importance because it can lead to:
Enrichment Opportunities
The enrichment opportunities students have in PSHE at Walton High ensures that they build critical life skills like resilience, empathy, and collaboration. We give our students the following opportunities:
Active democracy and leadership roles: The Lead Prefect roles, Student Council and Student Committees give students ownership to improve the student experience for all at the school. The Debate Society allows students to gain the knowledge, skills and confidence to be become active citizens in the democracy of our country.
Community Volunteering and Intergenerational Projects: Visits by local residential care homes to our school cultivate social responsibility and allow students to feel a sense of ‘giving back’ to our local community. Our increasing work with local food banks also teaches students the importance of caring for all in our community, especially the most vulnerable.
Careers and Enterprise Initiatives: Interactive Work Tree events meeting local employers, entrepreneurs and public sector workers from Milton Keynes allows students to consider future careers and the pathways to get there.
Personal Growth: Allows students to consider the values they have and the kind of person they want to be through workshops on addiction, Progressive Masculinity and the JJ Effect.
The Duke of Edinburgh’s Award (DofE): Gives students the experience of an external residential and expedition programme that heavily build youth resilience, navigation skills, and teamwork.
Student Voice is essential in PSHE because it bridges the gap between our curriculum goals and students lived experiences. It ensures that learning remains highly relevant, timely, and supportive of their immediate wellbeing and safety needs.
We ensure that the Student Voice in PSHE at Walton High enables to consider the following:
Lived Relevance: Society and online media evolve rapidly. By listening to students, we can gain insights into the digital spaces, language, and trends directly impacting their lives.
Targeted Support: Gathering feedback allows individual teachers to tailor lessons to their specific class needs, identify gaps in knowledge, and address sensitive topics (such as RSE) in a way that respects diverse perspectives and backgrounds.
Safeguarding: Having a culture where students feel they are listened to empowers them to raise concerns and allows the school to notice wellbeing or safety issues early, before they escalate.
